title: Dashboard
description: Overview of your infrastructure: server status, pipeline activity, and pending tasks.

sections.title: Status Cards
sections.content: The top row displays key metrics: total servers, online/offline count, and pending tasks. They update automatically when agents report status changes over the real-time connection.

sections.title: Recent Activity
sections.content: The lower section lists your servers with their status and the most recent pipeline runs with their results. Click any item to open its detail page.

sections.title: Custom Dashboards
sections.content: Administrators can build custom dashboards with widgets and set one as the default home view. See the Custom Dashboards article for details.

title: Servers
description: Manage your fleet of servers - monitor status, view metrics, and configure agents.

sections.title: Server List
sections.content: Browse all registered servers with filters by type (Normal, Build, Docker) and status (Online, Offline). Use the search bar to find a server by name or hostname.

sections.title: Server Detail
sections.content: Open a server to see its overview, system metrics (CPU, RAM, Disk), installed services, Docker containers, projects, pipelines, releases, tasks, and logs, organized into sections.

sections.title: Services
sections.content: From the Services section you manage detected modules - Docker, Apache, Certbot, Mail, TeamSpeak, Portsentry, Rkhunter - and run install, start, and stop actions. Results stream back in real time.

sections.title: Agent Enrollment
sections.content: Servers appear automatically when an agent enrolls using a registration token. Generate a token from the Add Agent wizard, then run the generated install command on the target machine.

title: Projects
description: Organize your work into projects with Git repositories, environments, and deployment pipelines.

sections.title: Creating Projects
sections.content: Create a project by providing a name, optional description, and Git repository URL. Projects can be tagged for easy filtering and belong to an organization.

sections.title: Project Sections
sections.content: Each project groups its pipelines, target servers, releases, artifacts, variable libraries, vaults, environments, tasks, logs, and Git repository into dedicated sections.

sections.title: Project Management
sections.content: Edit project settings or remove projects you no longer need. Each project shows the number of associated pipelines and the status of their last run.

title: Git Repositories
description: Browse the Git repositories linked to your projects - branches, commits, and history.

sections.title: Browsing Repositories
sections.content: Inspect a project's repository: list branches, view recent commits, and open a commit to see its details. The view is read-only and built for quickly checking what changed.

sections.title: Local Mirror
sections.content: Repositories are mirrored locally, so browsing stays fast and keeps working even when the upstream host is slow or temporarily unavailable. Pipelines clone from the same mirror.

title: Environments
description: Define deployment environments such as Development, Staging, and Production for a project.

sections.title: Managing Environments
sections.content: Create environments per project to represent your deployment targets. Give each one a clear name so it is obvious where a pipeline deploys.

sections.title: Using Environments
sections.content: Pipelines reference an environment to scope where a release is deployed, making it easy to track which version is live in each stage of your delivery flow.

title: Pipelines
description: Define and run CI/CD pipelines with stages, steps, and variables.

sections.title: Pipeline Definition
sections.content: Pipelines are defined in YAML with stages and steps (Azure DevOps-style stages > jobs > steps). Use the visual editor for drag-and-drop design, or edit the YAML directly with syntax validation.

sections.title: Running Pipelines
sections.content: Trigger pipelines manually, via webhooks, or on a schedule. Follow progress in real time with live log streaming. Each run shows stage-by-stage status and durations.

sections.title: Variables and Secrets
sections.content: Attach variable libraries and vaults to a pipeline. Variables are substituted at runtime. Use the dry-run to preview the resolved commands before executing for real.

title: Pipeline Templates
description: Reusable pipeline templates to standardize your deployment workflows.

sections.title: Using Templates
sections.content: Create templates from existing pipelines or from scratch. When creating a new pipeline, pick a template to pre-populate stages and steps. Templates are versioned with changelog entries.

title: Variable Libraries
description: Shared key-value stores for pipeline variables, reusable across multiple pipelines.

sections.title: Managing Entries
sections.content: Add, edit, or delete key-value entries. Changes are versioned - view the history to see previous values and who made each change. A library belongs to an organization or a project.

sections.title: Using in Pipelines
sections.content: Link a library to a pipeline, then reference its values with $(key) syntax in your steps. Use the copy button to grab the exact key reference.

title: Vaults
description: Encrypted secret storage for sensitive values like API keys, passwords, and tokens.

sections.title: Secret Management
sections.content: Secrets are encrypted with AES-256 at rest. Add a secret with a key and value - values are masked in the UI and in logs. View the version history to audit changes.

sections.title: Using Secrets in Pipelines
sections.content: Link a vault to a pipeline and reference secrets with $(secret.key) syntax. Secrets are resolved at execution time and automatically masked in log output.

title: Releases
description: Track software releases across your projects with build status and promotion workflows.

sections.title: Release Detection
sections.content: Releases are detected automatically from Git tags. Use Sync to fetch new releases on demand. Each release shows its version, branch, and current status.

sections.title: Promotion and Rollback
sections.content: Promote a successful release to production or roll back to a previous version. Trigger the associated build pipelines directly from the release view.

title: Artifacts
description: Browse and download the build artifacts produced by your project pipelines.

sections.title: Artifact Storage
sections.content: Pipeline steps can publish artifacts such as build output, packages, or reports. Each artifact is listed with its name, size, and the run that produced it.

sections.title: Downloading Artifacts
sections.content: Download any artifact to inspect it locally or to deploy it manually. Artifacts stay attached to the run that created them for full traceability.

title: Tasks
description: View and manage task executions across all servers and pipelines.

sections.title: Task List
sections.content: Browse all tasks with filters by status, executor, and server. Each task shows its current status, the associated pipeline step, and its execution duration.

sections.title: Task Logs
sections.content: Open a task to view its output. Logs stream in real time for running tasks; completed task logs are stored and remain available for review.

title: Logs
description: Real-time log console with filtering, search, and color-coded log levels.

sections.title: Live Streaming
sections.content: Logs stream in real time over the SignalR connection. The console auto-scrolls to show new entries; use pause to freeze the view and examine specific lines.

sections.title: Filtering
sections.content: Filter logs by agent, pipeline, or level (Info, Warning, Error). Use the search box to find specific text within the displayed logs.

title: Alerts
description: Configure metric-based alerts to get notified when thresholds are exceeded.

sections.title: Creating Alerts
sections.content: Define an alert by selecting a metric (CPU, Memory, Disk), setting a threshold percentage, and choosing how long the condition must hold before it triggers.

sections.title: Alert Notifications
sections.content: When an alert fires, notifications are surfaced in the app and the unread count appears in the sidebar. Review active and past alerts from the alerts view.

title: Custom Dashboards
description: Create custom dashboards with configurable widgets (admin only).

sections.title: Widget Configuration
sections.content: Add widgets to a dashboard and configure their type, position, and size. Available widget types include charts, counters, and status indicators.

sections.title: Default Dashboard
sections.content: Mark a dashboard as default to show it on the home page, giving your team the view that matters most as soon as they sign in.

title: Organizations
description: Group servers, projects, and members under an organization with scoped ownership (admin only).

sections.title: Membership and Roles
sections.content: Each organization has members with roles, including Owner. Owners manage membership and settings. A default organization is created at first startup with the bootstrap administrator as its Owner.

sections.title: Scoped Ownership
sections.content: Servers, projects, plugin registrations, and registration tokens belong to an organization. Members see the resources of the organizations they belong to. When creating a resource you can pick its organization, or let it default to yours.

title: Roles
description: Define roles and resource-based permissions to control who can view or change each resource (admin only).

sections.title: Resource Permissions
sections.content: Permissions are granted per resource (server or project) and per action, such as read or write. Group permissions into roles and assign roles to users.

sections.title: Effective Access
sections.content: A user's effective access is the union of their direct resource permissions and the resources of their organizations. Changes take effect immediately as the permission cache refreshes.

title: Users
description: Manage user accounts, roles, and access permissions (admin only).

sections.title: User Management
sections.content: Create, edit, and delete user accounts. Reset a password when needed, and enable or require two-factor authentication for stronger account security.

sections.title: Roles and Permissions
sections.content: Assign roles to control what each user can access. Access is resource-based: a user only sees the servers and projects granted to them, directly or through their organizations. See the Roles article for details.

title: Plugins
description: Extend Aetheus functionality by registering and managing plugins (admin only).

sections.title: Plugin Management
sections.content: Register a plugin by providing its name, author, entry point, and type. Enable or disable plugins as needed, and unregister those that are no longer required.

title: Audit Logs
description: Track all changes made in the system for security and compliance (admin only).

sections.title: Browsing Audit Logs
sections.content: Filter audit entries by action type (Created, Updated, Deleted), entity type, date range, and user. Each entry records a timestamp, the action, the affected entity, and who made the change.

title: System Logs
description: Inspect the backend application logs for troubleshooting and diagnostics (admin only).

sections.title: Browsing System Logs
sections.content: View server-side application logs with their level, timestamp, and message. Use this to diagnose backend errors that are not tied to a specific agent task or pipeline run.

title: API Reference
description: Browse every backend API endpoint exposed by Aetheus, grouped by area (admin only).

sections.title: Browsing Endpoints
sections.content: The reference is generated from the live OpenAPI document, so it always matches the running backend. Endpoints are grouped by tag and show the HTTP method, path, and summary.

sections.title: Finding an Endpoint
sections.content: Use the search box to filter endpoints by path or description. This is the quickest way to discover the exact route and method for an integration.

title: Settings
description: Manage your profile, appearance, notifications, and account security.

sections.title: Profile and Appearance
sections.content: Set your display name, switch between the dark and light theme, and choose your language (English or French). Appearance preferences are saved in your browser.

sections.title: Notifications
sections.content: Choose which alerts you want to receive - email, pipeline, and server notifications - so the app surfaces only what matters to you.

sections.title: Security
sections.content: Change your password and enable two-factor authentication (TOTP) for an extra layer of protection on your account.
